metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to all contributions and all written communication on GitHub (pull requests, issues, discussions)

evidence.quote: We do not accept any contributions that contain content generated by LLMs.
We will close any pull request, issue, or discussion that does not comply to this policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named; only enforcement (closing) stated
domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans LLM-generated content in contributions and clarifies scope by naming pull requests, issues, and discussions, giving a clear supervision level (banned) and scope. However, it never states who is answerable for the content submitted (e.g. the contributor); it only states that maintainers will close non-compliant items, which is enforcement, not accountability. Per the rules this makes the domain 'partial' rather than 'yes'.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md contains no reference to meetings, recordings, or notetaker/meeting bots of any kind.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule naming documentation, blogs, or design assets specifically
domains.reasoning: The AI policy names 'contributions' and 'written communication on GitHub' (clarified elsewhere as PRs/issues/discussions), but never names documentation, blog posts, or design assets. A reader could wonder whether documentation PRs fall under the code_contributions ban, but the text does not name content as its own category, so this domain is not addressed as defined.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The document states maintainers will close non-compliant PRs/issues/discussions, but this is enforcement of the LLM-content ban, not a rule about whether AI may be used to perform moderation actions. No supervision level or accountability for AI-assisted moderation is stated.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted review of contributions
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md does not discuss whether reviewers may use AI tools to review contributions; only the submission side (contributors not using LLM-generated content) is addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic interaction with repository
domains.reasoning: There is no mention of autonomous agents or bots acting on the repository independently; the policy only addresses human contributors submitting LLM-generated content.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or carbon impact
domains.reasoning: No language in the document references environmental cost of AI tools as a rationale or a rule.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: No language references infrastructure strain, hardware cost, or financing tied to AI use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on project's own data being used for AI training
domains.reasoning: The policy only concerns receiving LLM-generated content, not whether the project's own contributions, issues, or discussions may be used as training data for models.

unscoped_statements.quote: We do not accept any contributions that contain content generated by LLMs. This also includes all written communication on GitHub.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The project bans all LLM-generated content in contributions and GitHub communication (PRs, issues, discussions), enforced by closing non-compliant items, but never assigns accountability for compliance and is entirely silent on notetaker bots, standalone content categories like docs/blogs/design assets, moderation, review, autonomous agent use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training-data reuse.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
